#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mint a release tag as an ANNOTATED tag pushed with a CI-firing token, and
# verify the tag train actually started (gh-2026). Shared by the two
# draft-capable create paths:
#
#   - scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh (build-macos.yml release-macos,
#     build-mobile.yml release-mobile) — the tag was DEFINITELY missing at
#     attach time;
#   - scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh (build-macos.yml build-macos-cli /
#     build-extension) — a `gh release create` for a missing ref would
#     REST-mint a lightweight API tag with NO push event (the v0.1.408
#     silent class, issue #597): no tag train, a stranded draft.
#
# Why this exists — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 stale drafts (gh-2026): the
# release legs pushed the annotated tag through the GH_TOKEN URL, but
# actions/checkout had already persisted the JOB token in the repo-local
# git config as `http.<host>/.extraheader = AUTHORIZATION: basic …`. That
# header outranks the URL-embedded credentials on the wire, so GitHub saw
# a GITHUB_TOKEN push — and GitHub NEVER fires workflow runs for
# GITHUB_TOKEN pushes (gh-1172; docs/ci.md "its token triggers the
# tag-scoped jobs, which GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never do"). Both legs stayed
# green, no tag run ever existed on the refs, the provenance-owned publish
# (gh-1801) never ran, and the daily sweeper deleted the drafts a day
# later. Two guards close the class:
#
#   1. strip the persisted extraheader(s) before the push — the same
#      cleanup the Actions runner's post-job step performs ("Removing HTTP
#      extra header") — so the URL's PAT credentials are what GitHub sees
#      and the push fires ci.yml's `push: tags: ['v*']` train;
#   2. verify the outcome: poll for any workflow run on the tag ref within
#      a bounded budget. A push that triggers nothing fails this script
#      LOUD (no draft is created — the caller never reaches its create
#      step), so the leg goes red with a self-explaining error instead of
#      stranding a draft for the sweeper.
#
# Usage: release_tag_mint.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB, GITHUB_SHA (Actions
#      defaults), GH_TOKEN — a PAT/App token, NEVER the workflow
#      GITHUB_TOKEN (a GITHUB_TOKEN push succeeds but can never trigger
#      the train; static lint pins every call site's export).
#      RELEASE_TARGET_SHA overrides the tag target (defaults GITHUB_SHA).
#      RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES (default 12) ×
#      RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) bound the
#      verification; the test harness shrinks both.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_tag_mint.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# Fail fast BEFORE the cryptic crash: the push URL below collapses to ''
# when GH_TOKEN is unset, and git's `fatal: bad repository ''` does not
# point at the env gap (run 39766453580, v1.0.626 mobile leg).
if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::error::tag $tag is missing but GH_TOKEN is not set — the annotated-tag push would run 'git push \"\"'. Set GH_TOKEN (PAT/App token) on the calling step, or the tag can never be minted here." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Guard 1 — strip the persisted checkout credentials. actions/checkout
# (persist-credentials defaults true) leaves the job token as an
# `http.<host>/.extraheader` in the LOCAL git config; git sends that
# Authorization header on every request to the host, and it outranks the
# URL-embedded GH_TOKEN credentials — the minted push would authenticate
# as GITHUB_TOKEN and the train would never fire (gh-2026). Unset every
# extraheader key the same way the runner's post-job cleanup does.
while IFS= read -r extraheader_key; do
  [ -n "$extraheader_key" ] || continue
  git config --local --unset-all "$extraheader_key" || true
done < <(git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'http\..*\.extraheader' 2>/dev/null || true)

# Guard 1b — actions/checkout ≥ v7 (gh-2039, run 41393469972) no longer
# writes the job token as a repo-local extraheader key at all: it writes
# a `git-credentials-<uuid>.config` file under RUNNER_TEMP and references
# it from repo-local `includeIf.gitdir:<gitdir>.path` entries. The sweep
# above then no-ops: `--get-regexp` LISTS the key (git resolves it
# through the include) but the key only EXISTS in the included file, so
# the repo-local unset fails silently under `|| true`. Remove every
# includeIf entry pointing at a credentials config file and delete the
# file — exactly what the runner's post-job cleanup does ("Removing
# includeIf entries pointing to credentials config files").
stripped_v7=0
while IFS= read -r include_key; do
  [ -n "$include_key" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r include_val; do
    [ -n "$include_val" ] || continue
    case "$include_val" in
      *git-credentials-*.config)
        git config --local --unset-all "$include_key" '.*git-credentials-[^/]*\.config$' || true
        rm -f "$include_val" 2>/dev/null || true
        stripped_v7=1
        ;;
    esac
  done < <(git config --local --get-all "$include_key" 2>/dev/null || true)
done < <(git config --local --name-only --get-regexp 'includeIf\.gitdir:' 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$stripped_v7" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "stripped checkout v7 persisted credentials (includeIf entries + git-credentials config files)"
fi

# Guard 1c — fail loud if an Authorization header STILL resolves for
# github.com after both strips (a scope this script cannot unset: the
# runner user's global/system gitconfig, or a brand-new checkout
# persistence shape). Pushing anyway would authenticate as the
# GITHUB_TOKEN class and strand the release for the sweeper a day later;
# a red leg naming the residual header is the actionable outcome.
residual_header="$(git config --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$residual_header" ]; then
  residual_origin="$(git config --show-origin --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\t.*//' | head -n1)"
  echo "::error::a persisted Authorization header still resolves for github.com after the strip (${residual_origin:-unknown origin}) — the minted push would authenticate as the CI-suppressed token and no tag train could fire. Remove it (e.g. git config --global --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader) and re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi

target="${RELEASE_TARGET_SHA:-${GITHUB_SHA:?}}"
echo "tag $tag missing — minting annotated tag at $target (token-URL push, fires the tag train)"
git fetch origin "$target" --depth=1 2>/dev/null || git fetch origin main --depth=50
# CI checkout carries no identity; annotate as the actions bot without
# touching global config (empty ident → exit 128, run 35426119831).
git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" \
    -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
    tag -a "$tag" -m "Release $tag" "$target"
# The push is NOT race-idempotent: tags never fast-forward, and the daily
# flow has up to ~5 parallel minters converging on the same missing tag
# (build-macos-cli's two arch legs plus build-extension and both attach
# legs). The loser's push is rejected ("already exists") — that is a WIN
# (a sibling leg minted the same commit), never a failure. Re-probe the
# ref before failing: present → continue to train verification; still
# absent → the push genuinely failed (credential, perms, incident) and
# the leg must go red with a self-explaining error.
if ! git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" "refs/tags/$tag"; then
  if git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "tag $tag was minted concurrently by a sibling leg — continuing to train verification"
  else
    echo "::error::tag $tag push failed and the ref is still missing — the push itself failed (credential, permissions, or a GitHub incident), not a race with a sibling leg. No draft will be created; fix the push and re-run." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Guard 2 — the train must actually start. A push that fires no workflow
# run (a GITHUB_TOKEN-classed credential on the wire, a GitHub incident, a
# workflow-file mismatch at the tag commit) silently strands every draft
# attached to the tag: green legs, no publish, the sweeper cleans up a day
# later (v1.0.663 / v1.0.665). The run row for the push event appears
# within seconds; poll briefly and fail loud.
tries="${RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES:-12}"
sleep_s="${RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_SLEEP:-10}"
runs_seen=0
for _ in $(seq 1 "$tries"); do
  sleep "$sleep_s"
  # A probe failure must NOT read as "no train": gh prefers GH_TOKEN (the
  # RELEASE_PAT) for this call, so a fine-grained PAT without Actions:read,
  # an expired PAT, or a rate limit all land here. Swallowing the error
  # (2>/dev/null || echo 0) burns the whole budget and then blames the push
  # credential — a misleading RCA on a red release leg. Fail fast and
  # surface the probe's own output instead.
  # gh can exit 0 yet write a warning to stderr (deprecation/upgrade
  # notice, config warning); merging stderr into the captured value would
  # corrupt the numeric check below ("integer expression expected") and
  # read as "no train" — rolling back a possibly-live tag over a benign
  # warning. Keep stderr OUT of the success value; surface it only on the
  # failure path.
  probe_err="$(mktemp)"
  probe_out="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 10 \
    --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>"$probe_err")" || {
    echo "::error::train verification probe failed for $tag (gh run list): $(cat "$probe_err") — a failing probe (RELEASE_PAT without Actions:read, expired PAT, rate limit) is NOT evidence of a suppressed train; fix the probe credential before re-running." >&2
    rm -f "$probe_err"
    exit 1
  }
  rm -f "$probe_err"
  if [ "${probe_out:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    runs_seen=1
    break
  fi
done
if [ "$runs_seen" -ne 1 ]; then
  # Roll the untrained tag back before failing: the pushed ref left in
  # place would make the prescribed "fix the credential and re-run" skip
  # the mint (and its train check) entirely — the caller's plain
  # `gh release create --draft` would then attach a draft to a ref whose
  # train never ran, silently re-arming the exact stranded-draft shape
  # this script exists to prevent (v1.0.663 / v1.0.665). Drop the LOCAL
  # tag object too: a reused self-hosted workspace would otherwise die at
  # `git tag -a` on the re-run.
  echo "::warning::rolling back the untrained tag ref so a fixed re-run can re-mint" >&2
  git push "${GH_TOKEN:+https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" ":refs/tags/$tag" ||
    echo "::warning::rollback of refs/tags/$tag failed — a re-run will skip the mint (tag exists) and can strand the draft; delete refs/tags/$tag manually before re-running" >&2
  git tag -d "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  echo "::error::tag train did not start for $tag: pushed refs/tags/$tag to ${repo} but no workflow run appeared on the ref within the verification budget — the push likely authenticated as a CI-suppressed token (GitHub never fires workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes; the persisted actions/checkout extraheader must not outrank the GH_TOKEN push credentials), or the tag-trigger filter does not match. No draft was created; fix the push credential and re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ tag train for $tag started (workflow run visible on the ref) — the draft publish path is live"

  "key": "pr-2041",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-2039 [daily-publish] cli leg failed",
    "description": "Closes #2039
### Root Cause
The cli leg failed in two independent jobs:
- **Tag-train failure (Build macOS CLI arm64)**: actions/checkout **v7** no longer persists the job token as a repo-local `http.<host>/.extraheader` key — it writes a `git-credentials-<uuid>.config` file under RUNNER_TEMP referenced by repo-local `includeIf.gitdir:` entries. `release_tag_mint.sh` Guard 1 only unset repo-local keys, so the strip silently no-op'd, the Authorization header still outranked the URL-embedded RELEASE_PAT credentials, GitHub classed the push as GITHUB_TOKEN, and no tag train ever fired for v1.0.682 (the filter itself is healthy — v1.0.681's train fired the same day).
- **Codesign failure (Build macOS x86_64)**: `xcode_backend`'s raw `codesign --sign <SHA-1>` depends on ambient persistent-keychain state that nothing re-asserts on the no-sandbox path — "no identity found" 7m02s after the last keychain activity, while the identity itself was verified valid at 06:07 and signed the DMG at 06:27. The arm64 leg passed only because its arm64-only TestFlight PKG step incidentally re-ran `ci-sign install` right before its own build.

### Fix
- `scripts/release_tag_mint.sh`: Guard 1b removes `includeIf.gitdir:` entries pointing at `git-credentials-*.config` files and deletes those files (mirrors the runner's own post-job cleanup); Guard 1c fails loud BEFORE pushing if an Authorization header still resolves for github.com (naming the residual origin).
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (no-sandbox step): gated `~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos` at point of use before the build (idempotent re-assert: unlock + identity verify + search-list rewrite; self-heals via the CI_SIGN_P12_* env if the identity is genuinely gone), for BOTH archs.
- `flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh`: pre-flight `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` against the pinned identity before the multi-minute flutter build — a miss now fails in ~1s with the exact remediation instead of after a 5-minute build.

### Test Coverage
- `test/release_tag_mint_test.dart`: new v7-credentials test (header must no longer resolve, credentials file deleted, tag still lands) — failed before the fix, passes after; new Guard 1c negative (global-scope residual header → abort before any push/probe); 7/7 mint tests pass.
- `test/ci_macos_nosandbox_point_of_use_sign_test.dart` (new): AC1 point-of-use re-assert ordering, AC2 pre-flight presence/ordering.
- Full suite: see run log — no regressions.

### Notes
- The v1.0.682 draft created by the sibling `build-extension` leg (it saw the tag existing before the rollback and skipped the mint) is reclaimed by the daily sweeper (issue #282); the rolled-back ref makes the next run re-mint correctly.
- Guard 1c intentionally reds a leg when an un-strippable Authorization header exists — that push can never fire the train, and a red leg naming the origin is the actionable outcome."

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the

# gh-2039 pre-flight — the pinned identity must be resolvable by the
# SAME search list codesign reads, BEFORE the multi-minute flutter
# build whose xcode_backend codesign is the first real consumer. A
# missing/locked/expired identity used to surface as `error: no
# identity found` 5+ minutes into the build (run 41393469972); fail
# here in ~1s with the exact remediation instead.
#
# No `-v` (gh-2039 rework review): the verbose listing includes INVALID
# identities too, each with its failure reason (e.g.
# CSSMERR_TP_CERT_EXPIRED) AND its SHA-1 — an expired pinned identity
# would match the grep and the exact "expired cert" case this guard
# exists to catch would slip into the 5-minute build. The plain
# listing is VALID identities only, which is also the closer
# approximation of what codesign will accept. `-i` because
# `codesign --sign <SHA1>` and ci-sign's validity check are
# case-insensitive — the pre-flight must be no stricter than its
# consumers.
if [[ "$identity" != "-" ]]; then
  if ! security find-identity -p codesigning 2>/dev/null | grep -Fiq -- "$identity"; then
    echo "::error::signing identity '$identity' is not resolvable as a VALID identity via 'security find-identity -p codesigning' (missing, expired, or the signing keychain is locked) — codesign inside 'flutter build' would fail after a full build. Re-assert the signing state first: ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos (unlock + identity verify + search-list rewrite), then re-run." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[build_macos_nosandbox] identity pre-flight OK: '$identity' resolvable for codesigning"
fi

# Thread: pre-flight matches invalid identities too (⚠️ IMPORTANT)

**Fixed.** The expired-identity gap is closed — `flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh:67` no longer consults the verbose listing.

## What changed

```bash
# before
if ! security find-identity -v -p codesigning 2>/dev/null | grep -F -- "$identity" >/dev/null; then
# after
if ! security find-identity -p codesigning 2>/dev/null | grep -Fiq -- "$identity"; then
```

- Dropped `-v` — the pre-flight now consults the **valid-identities-only** listing, so an expired pinned identity (listed under `-v` with its SHA-1 + `CSSMERR_TP_CERT_EXPIRED`) can no longer satisfy the guard and slip into the 5-minute build. The error text was updated to match ("not resolvable as a VALID identity via `security find-identity -p codesigning`") so the message documents what the guard actually enforces.
- Applied nit 1: `grep -Fiq` — the pre-flight is now case-insensitive, no stricter than its consumers (`codesign --sign <SHA1>`, `scripts/ci-sign:204` uses `grep -qi`). The earlier identity-*discovery* blocks in the same script legitimately keep `-v` (they read identity *names*, which only the verbose listing carries).

## Tests (TDD)

- `test/ci_macos_nosandbox_point_of_use_sign_test.dart` AC2 was rewritten: it now isolates the gh-2039 pre-flight block (not the earlier discovery block) and asserts the valid-only command, the absence of `find-identity -v` in the block, `grep -Fiq`, and the corrected error text. The pinned `security find-identity -v -p codesigning` string is gone (nit 2).
- New executable AC3: a stubbed `security` exposes the pinned SHA-1 **only** in its `-v` listing (tagged `CSSMERR_TP_CERT_EXPIRED`), the valid-only listing is empty, and a stubbed `flutter` records any invocation. Failed before the fix (pre-flight passed, flutter build was reached), passes after (exit ≠ 0, `::error::`, flutter never invoked). Mutation-verified: reverting to `-v` + `grep -F` re-reds AC3.

# Thread: P12 secret + password sit in the step env for every child process (💡 SUGGESTION)

**No code change — concurring with your own assessment ("informational … No action required for this PR"), and deferring the file-based channel rather than hand-rolling one here.**

Rationale against acting in this PR:

- The exposure shape is identical to the existing, already-reviewed provisioning step (`build-macos.yml` line ~549), which passes the same two secrets the same way (`CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV` indirection). Changing only the *new* call site would leave the older one as the dominant blast radius — the hardening only pays off when both move together.
- GitHub log-masking covers both values (`MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64` / `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` are registered secrets), so the multi-minute build window adds no log-leak path; the residual risk is an env-dumping child process, which is a property of the step, not of this change.
- Scoping the P12 to the `identity gone` branch requires `ci-sign` to grow a file-based secret channel (`CI_SIGN_P12_B64_FILE`) — a `scripts/ci-sign` interface change with its own keychain-facing test surface (`test/ci_sign_host_keychain_guard_test.dart`), i.e. a separate scoped change, not a rider on this fix.

Re-verified against current head: the step env block is the only place the P12 secret is introduced on the no-sandbox path, it matches the provisioning step's indirection pattern verbatim, and AC1 in `test/ci_macos_nosandbox_point_of_use_sign_test.dart` keeps the re-assert gated on the pinned identity so unsigned/ad-hoc runs never see it. If the `CI_SIGN_P12_B64_FILE` channel lands later, both call sites should be migrated in the same change.

arguments.content:
# PR #2041 rework — review-thread fixes (gh-2039 follow-up)

## Issues/Notes

- **4 open review threads addressed**: 3 with code changes (threads 1–3), 1 informational thread resolved without changes per the reviewer's own "No action required" verdict (thread 4, rationale in `outputs/review_replies/thread_4_p12_env_scope.md`).
- **Owned CI violations: none.** `ci_violations.json` for the red head (`69c86304`, validation run 41409232519) reports `owned: 0`; no "Violations you must fix" table exists in `ci_failures.md`. The 5 failed checks were judged from the raw logs — none is attributable to a file this PR changes:

  | Check | Classification | Evidence |
  |---|---|---|
  | Build macOS (debug) | `disputed: transient runner-network failure, not the "CocoaPods layer / spec drift" the gate message claims` | Raw log: `pod install` **succeeded** (8.5s) and the build compiled for minutes before dying at the `sqlite3` native-asset hook — `HandshakeException: Connection terminated during handshake` downloading `libsqlite3.arm64.macos.dylib` from GitHub Releases. A TLS/network flake on the runner; nothing this PR touches (`Podfile`/`Podfile.lock`/sqlite3 untouched by the diff, and the fix cannot be produced from a Linux checkout — `pod install --repo-update` needs macOS). The next validation run on the pushed head re-tries it. |
  | Quality gate | inherited aggregate | Its log is the status collector echoing `build-macos = failure` — red solely because of the row above. |
  | Binaries smoke gate | foreign/infra, log unavailable | GitHub API returns `404 Not Found` for the job-log download; no attributable error exists. No binary/artifact path is changed by this PR. |
  | JS engine integration (quickjs-ng) | foreign/infra, log unavailable | Same 404; no JS-engine file is changed by this PR. |
  | Quality gate (second entry) | same aggregate as above | See above. |

- No merge conflicts (`merge_conflicts.md` absent, tree clean).

## Approach

Followed TDD (RED → GREEN → mutation checks) per finding, in review-thread order:

1. **Thread 1 (⚠️ IMPORTANT, `build_macos_nosandbox.sh:67`)** — `security find-identity -v` lists *invalid* identities too (each with its SHA-1 + failure reason), so an expired pinned identity satisfied the pre-flight and slipped into the 5-minute build. Dropped `-v` so the pre-flight consults the **valid-only** listing, and applied nit 1 (`grep -Fiq`) so the guard is case-insensitive like its consumers (`codesign --sign <SHA1>`, `scripts/ci-sign` `grep -qi`). Error text updated to name the command the guard actually runs. The earlier identity-*discovery* blocks keep `-v` legitimately (they read identity *names*). AC2 rewritten + new executable AC3 regression test (see Test Coverage).
2. **Thread 2 (💡, `release_tag_mint.sh:103`)** — widened the Guard 1b sweep regexp exactly as suggested: `'includeIf\.gitdir(/i)?:|^include\.path$'`, covering the case-insensitive `gitdir/i:` conditional variant and plain non-conditional `include.path`. The inner value-scoped `case`/`--unset-all` is untouched, so benign includes on the widened shapes cannot be over-stripped.
3. **Thread 3 (💡)** — added the benign-include survival coverage you sketched: fixture gains `includeIf.gitdir:$work/.git/benign.path` → a real `not-credentials.config` file on disk; the v7creds test now asserts the only surviving includeIf keys are benign, the benign key still resolves, and the file still exists. Mutation-verified: dropping the value regex reds the mixed-value `include.path` assertion; removing the value guard entirely reds the v7creds assertions.
4. **Thread 4 (💡)** — no code change (audit-resolve): the reviewer's own verdict is "informational … No action required for this PR"; scoping the P12 to the degraded branch needs a `ci-sign` `CI_SIGN_P12_B64_FILE` channel (interface change to `scripts/ci-sign` + its guard suite) and only pays off when the existing provisioning step (line ~549) migrates too. Reply documents the deferral and re-verification against current head.

CI root cause: no owned reds; the single actionable red (Build macOS debug) is a transient runner-network TLS failure inside the `sqlite3` native-asset download, evidenced above; the other four are its aggregate or log-unavailable foreign reds. The re-run on the new head (validate-fresh) re-tries them.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh` — pre-flight: `security find-identity -p codesigning` (valid-only), `grep -Fiq`, updated comment + `::error::` text.
- `scripts/release_tag_mint.sh` — Guard 1b sweep regexp widened to `includeIf\.gitdir(/i)?:|^include\.path$`; comment documents the shapes and the value-scoping guarantee.
- `test/ci_macos_nosandbox_point_of_use_sign_test.dart` — AC2 rewritten to isolate the gh-2039 pre-flight block (valid-only command, no `-v` in the block, `grep -Fiq`, corrected error text); new AC3 executable expired-identity regression test (stubbed `security`/`flutter`); header contract updated.
- `test/release_tag_mint_test.dart` — fixture: benign include entry + on-disk benign file (thread 3), `v7VariantShapes` fixture mode (`gitdir/i:` + mixed-value `include.path`, thread 2); v7creds test asserts benign survival; new variant-strip test.

## Test Coverage

All RED-first, then GREEN, plus mutation checks on the negative tests:

- `test/ci_macos_nosandbox_point_of_use_sign_test.dart` (3 tests) — AC2 failed before the fix (`-v` + `grep -F` in the pre-flight block); AC3 failed before the fix (expired identity passed the pre-flight, stubbed `flutter` was invoked) and passes after (exit ≠ 0, `::error::`, flutter never reached).
- `test/release_tag_mint_test.dart` (8 tests, was 7) — new variant test failed before the regexp widening (`gitdir/i:` credentials entry left in the config) and passes after; benign-survival assertions verified by two deliberate mutations (both re-red, then restored).
- Affected cluster: `dart test test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart test/release_lazy_draft_mint_test.dart test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/ci_sign_host_keychain_guard_test.dart test/ci_cert_sha1_pin_guard_test.dart test/build_macos_spm_lane_guard_test.dart test/ci_macos_debug_spm_lane_guard_test.dart` → **96/96 pass**.
- Full default-tag suite (`dart test`): run against the frozen tree after all fixes — result recorded in the PR comment post-run (validation CI re-runs it on the pushed head regardless).
- `shellcheck scripts/release_tag_mint.sh flutter_app/scripts/build_macos_nosandbox.sh` → clean; `dart analyze` on both test files → no issues; `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` → clean.
